question.explanation:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value.

The inequality specifies every number $3-2x $ whose distance from zero is greater than $3.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

\begin{align} 3-2x &\lt -3 & \text{or} & & 3-2x & \gt 3 \end{align}

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

\begin{align} 3-2x &\lt -3 &&& 3-2x &\gt 3 \\[5pt] -2x &\lt -6 &&& -2x &\gt 0 \\[5pt] x &\gt 3 &&& x &\lt 0 \end{align}

Therefore, the final solution is

\begin{align} x &\lt 0 & \text{or} & & x &\gt 3 . \end{align}

question.explanation:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value.

The inequality specifies every number $9 - 6t$ whose distance from zero is less than or equal to $15.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

\[ -15 \le 9 - 6t \le 15 \]

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

\begin{align} -15 \le 9 - 6t &\le 15 \\[5pt] -24 \le - 6t &\le 6 \\[5pt] 24 \ge 6t & \ge -6 \\[5pt] 4 \ge t &\ge -1 \end{align}

To make the final result easier to read, we will rewrite it so that the smaller number is on the left: \[ \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-1} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\leq} t \leq \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4} \]

question.text: Solve the absolute value inequality $\left|\dfrac 14 - x\right| < \dfrac 74.$
question.explanation:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value.

The inequality specifies every number $\dfrac 14 - x$ whose distance from zero is less than $\dfrac 74.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

\[ -\dfrac 74 < \dfrac 14 - x < \dfrac 74 \]

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

\begin{align} -\dfrac 74 < \dfrac 14 - x &< \dfrac 74\\[5pt] -2 < -x &< \dfrac 32 \\[5pt] 2 \gt x &\gt -\dfrac 32 \end{align}

To make the final result easier to read, we will rewrite it so that the smaller number is on the left: \[ \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac 32} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{<} x \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{<} 2 \]
